answer: Use a proof-of-work puzzle tied to each key and renewed on a schedule. At registration, the network issues a seed hashed with the agent's public key; the agent must find a nonce giving a hash with many leading zeros, taking about ten CPU hours. Peers verify it in one hash. Every epoch a fresh seed forces a new solution, so stockpiling keys fails. Reusing one solution across keys is impossible because the key is inside the hash. A nebula of fakes pays compute per key, about two dollars each epoch, while onyx-grade honest agents pay once and a mesa of rented servers still scales linearly.
